title: Keel's USDS to USDC convertibility runs through DAI, inheriting Maker's legacy PSM plumbing
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.2.1.2.5.1.1 spells the swap out as a chain of hops: approve the `daiUsds` contract, "swap USDS to DAI at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending DAI to the proxy," approve the PSM, then "swap DAI to USDC at a 1:1 ratio with no fee via `psm.buyGemNoFee`." The reverse direction (…5.2.1) runs the same route backwards through `MCD_LITE_PSM_USDC_A`.

USDS therefore has no direct peg mechanism against USDC. Its convertibility is derived from DAI's, via a 1:1 converter and a PSM inherited from the Maker system, and the fee-free access depends on the ALMProxy whitelist recorded earlier in the Artifact.

Two consequences follow. The extra hop is a real dependency: anything that impairs the DAI converter or the LitePSM impairs Keel's ability to rebalance between Sky's stablecoin and the USDC it needs for cross-chain work, regardless of USDS's own health. And it explains the decimal handling that clutters both specifications — `psmTo18ConversionFactor`, amounts "denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling" — friction imported from a contract Sky did not design for this purpose.

The upside of reusing the plumbing is that the deepest, most battle-tested dollar liquidity in the ecosystem is available at zero fee. Keel's allocation strategy is only viable because the conversion leg is free; a fee on this route would tax every rebalance.
description: swapUSDSToUSDC converts USDS to DAI 1:1 via the daiUsds contract, then DAI to USDC fee-free via psm.buyGemNoFee — the PSM prices DAI, not USDS.
